Subject: Evidence request — employee clearance, training and leaver artifacts

Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. As part of Midtown Bank's SIG/SOC 2 review we need a short collection of artifacts that demonstrate your onboarding and offboarding controls for personnel. Specifically we need:  

- Examples of redacted background check reports for three hires (redactions acceptable; please keep PII removed)
- Training completion roster showing security awareness and data handling completion for the last 12 months
- Export of deprovisioning/audit logs for last 6 months (user deprovision events, timestamped)
- A brief vendor chain-of-custody statement for your background-check provider
- Any documented onboarding playbook that shows role-based access provisioning steps

Can you confirm: (1) what redaction standard you will follow, (2) whether the logs contain timestamps and actor IDs, and (3) an ETA for secure delivery? Midtown's compliance team would like this by EOD Friday, 2026-05-21 if possible.

If there are any restrictions on what you can share, flag them — we can accept redacted and hashed identifiers where needed.

Regards,
Lara Singh

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (HR ops) and Marcus (Security Ops) who will help assemble the artifacts. Quick answers up front:  

1) Redaction standard: we will remove PII fields (SSN, DOB, home address) and replace names with hashed identifiers; we can include a mapping file hashed with SHA-256 if you need consistent pseudonyms.
2) Logs: deprovisioning events include timestamp (UTC), actor (service account or admin ID), and the target username; we can export as CSV.
3) ETA: we can stage redacted samples and the training roster for review by 2026-05-20 EOD and provide full export by 2026-05-21 EOD. If you need faster turnaround on anything specific please call.

Monica — can you attach the sample redacted BG, the training roster (CSV), and the last 6 months deprovision export? Marcus — please include the vendor chain-of-custody statement and any SSO audit notes we can share.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
